ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the segment \(AC=6\,cm\), the segment \(BC=15\,cm\), point M is the midpoint of \(AC\), and a point N is taken on \(CB\) such that \(CN=\frac{1}{2}NB\). What is the length of \(MN\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $AC=6\,\text{cm}$,\\
it follows that $MC=\frac{1}{2}AC=\frac{1}{2}\times 6=3\,\text{cm}$,\\
since $CN=\frac{1}{2}NB$ and $BC=15\,\text{cm}$,\\
then $CN=\frac{1}{3}BC=\frac{1}{3}\times 15=5\,\text{cm}$,\\
therefore, $MN=MC+NC=3\,\text{cm}+5\,\text{cm}=\boxed{8\,\text{cm}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a single horizontal straight line with points ordered from left to right as A, M, C, N, B. Thus M lies between A and C, N lies between C and B, and segment MN consists of MC plus CN along the same line. Reasoning: Since M is the midpoint of AC and AC = 6 cm, MC = 6/2 = 3 cm.
